title: Affine and principal neighbourhood criterion for a Koszul-regular closed immersion
statement: Let $a:T\to W$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_W\to a_*\mathcal O_T)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Say that $\mathcal J$ is locally Koszul-regular along $a(T)$ if, for every $t\in T$, there is an open neighbourhood $N$ of $a(t)$ and finitely many sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal O_W(N)$ generating $\mathcal J|_N$, whose germs in $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ form a Koszul-regular sequence for every $w\in N$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Empty sequences are allowed. This condition is equivalent to the following: for every $t\in T$ and every open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of $a(t)$ there is an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq O$ containing $a(t)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] such that $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ over $U$ and $J$ is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence in $B$. If $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ over $W$, the latter neighbourhoods can be required to be principal opens $U=D(h)=\operatorname{Spec}A_h$, where $h\notin\mathfrak p$ for the prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $a(t)$ and $J=IA_h$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. No Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Assume the stated local condition. Fix $t$ and $O$, and choose its witness $N,s_1,\ldots,s_r$. By the affine basis choose $a(t)\in U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq N\cap O$. The closed-immersion affine criterion gives $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ over $U$, with $J=\mathcal J(U)$; the ideal-sheaf statement gives $\mathcal J|_U=\widetilde J$. Put $b_i=s_i|_U\in B$. The $b_i$ generate $\widetilde J$ as a sheaf, and their germs are Koszul-regular at every point of $U$.

source.place: Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme); divisors.tex Tag 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme), first shrinking paragraph

proof.text: On $\operatorname{Spec}B$, associated sheafification preserves kernels by finite-limit preservation and cokernels by the colimit clause of the tilde adjunction. Hence it preserves images (kernels of cokernels) and the quotient $\ker(d)/\operatorname{im}(d)$ defining homology. It reflects a zero module: $\widetilde M=0$ implies $M=\Gamma(U,\widetilde M)=0$ by the unit isomorphism. In particular it reflects exactness and surjectivity. These are direct kernel/cokernel calculations from the cited statements.

source.place: Tags 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), final assertion, and 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent); the exactness argument used in divisors.tex Tag 063G

proof.text: The map $B^r\to J$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i b_i$, sheafifies to the surjection $\mathcal O_U^r\to\mathcal J|_U$: the free-module identification sends the standard basis to the standard sections, and the tilde adjunction identifies the map by its sections. Step 2 reflects surjectivity, so $J=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$. The sheafification of $K_B(b)$ has finite free terms with increasing-wedge bases and differential matrices $d(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q})=\sum_j(-1)^{j+1}b_{i_j}e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\widehat e_{i_j}\cdots\wedge e_{i_q}$. At a point $w$ its stalk has these same matrices with $b_i$ replaced by its germ, so is $K_{\mathcal O_{W,w}}(b_w)$. These complexes are exact in positive degrees by the hypothesis. Exactness on stalks gives positive exactness of the sheaf complex; step 2 reflects this to $K_B(b)$. Thus $b$ is Koszul-regular by definition, proving the affine assertion.

source.place: divisors.tex Tag 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme), exactness argument; Tags 01HV and 01I7; modules.tex Tag 01AG

proof.text: Conversely choose such an affine $U$ at $a(t)$ (take $O=W$), and Koszul-regular generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $J$. The ideal-sheaf statement identifies $\mathcal J|_U$ with $\widetilde J$; the tilde adjunction and its colimit clause send the generating surjection $B^r\to J$ to the generating surjection $\mathcal O_U^r\to\mathcal J|_U$. For every $w\in U$ the structure stalk is $B_{\mathfrak q}$ by the affine stalk identification. This is flat over $B$ by localization flatness. Flat base change of Koszul regularity makes the germs of $b$ Koszul-regular in that stalk. Thus $N=U$ and these sections witness the original condition at $t$.

source.place: divisors.tex Tag 063G, converse; Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), (6),(7); algebra.tex Tag 00HT; more-algebra.tex Tag 062H

proof.text: Now suppose $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Start with the affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq O$ of step 3. The distinguished-open basis of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ gives $h\notin\mathfrak p$ with $a(t)\in D_A(h)\subseteq U$. Write $b=h|_U\in B$. The unit-germ description of a basic open shows $D_U(b)=D_A(h)$, since the latter is contained in $U$ and restriction leaves germs unchanged. The affine localization statement identifies this open both with $\operatorname{Spec}A_h$ and with $\operatorname{Spec}B_b$, using the actual restriction maps.

The quasi-coherent ideal sheaf restricted to this principal open has section ideal $JB_b$ when computed in $U$, and $IA_h$ when computed in $W$. Indeed the two basic-open localization clauses for a quasi-coherent module say precisely that its sections are the localization of its affine sections; applied to $\mathcal J$, the fraction $j/b^n$ maps to $b^{-n}j|_{D(b)}$, so its image inside $B_b$ is $JB_b$, and likewise over $A$. The ring identification in step 5 therefore identifies these two ideals. Since $B\to B_b$ is flat, the images of the generators from step 3 are Koszul-regular by flat base change and generate $JB_b$. Regard them in $A_h$ via that ring identification. The closed-immersion affine criterion identifies the inverse image with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_h/IA_h)$ over $D(h)$. This proves the required principal refinement inside the originally specified $O$.

source.place: Tags 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), (4),(5), 01I3 and 01IN; algebra.tex Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization); more-algebra.tex Tag 062H (lemma-koszul-regular-flat-base-change)

proof.text: Principal witnesses are affine witnesses by the principal-open affineness statement, so they imply the condition already proved equivalent in steps 1--4. All arguments allow $r=0$: the generating map is $0\to J$, and the Koszul complex has only its degree-zero term. If $T$ is empty the assertions quantified over $t$ are vacuous. No step assumes any finiteness condition on the ring beyond the given finite list of generators.

The split follows the source's route: tilde on an affine shrink, which preserves and reflects exactness. Step 1 takes an affine U inside N∩O by 01IT; the cover criterion and the ideal-sheaf node give a^-1U=Spec(B/J) with J=𝒥(U) and 𝒥|_U equal to the tilde of J. Step 2 (elementary) is correct: tilde preserves kernels by the finite-limit node and cokernels by adjunction clause (4), and the unit isomorphism makes it reflect zero modules. Step 3 is correct: the generating map is the tilde of B^r→J under the adjunction, so J=(b). The tilde Koszul complex is free with the explicit Koszul matrices, its stalks are the Koszul complexes of the germs, and stalk exactness (module-stalk-exact (5)) reflects to H_i(K_B(b))=0 for i≥1. Step 4 uses stalks B_q, flatness of localization and 062H; it covers every point of U, including points off a(T). Step 5: D_U(h|_U)=D_A(h) holds by the unit-germ description, and affine-ideals (0) identifies the ring of this open with both A_h and B_b. Step 6 uses basic-open-localization (1) to get 𝒥(D(b))=JB_b and 𝒥(D(h))=IA_h, then flat base change, a ring isomorphism and the cover criterion. I tested V(x)⊂Spec k[x], r=0, a unit generator, T empty and the sequence (0) over a field, and the item needs no Noetherian hypothesis. lean.statement: theorem koszulClosedImmersion_affine_criterion {T W : Scheme.{u}} (a : T ⟶ W) [IsClosedImmersion a] : (∀ t : T, ∃ N : W.Opens, a t ∈ N ∧ ∃ (r : ℕ) (s : Fin r → Γ(W, N)), (∀ (V : W.affineOpens) (hVN : V.1 ≤ N), Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ W.presheaf.map (homOfLE hVN).op (s i))) = a.ker.ideal V) ∧ (∀ (w : W) (hw : w ∈ N), RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular (fun i ↦ W.presheaf.germ N w hw (s i)))) ↔ (∀ (t : T) (O : W.Opens), a t ∈ O → ∃ U : W.affineOpens, a t ∈ U.1 ∧ U.1 ≤ O ∧ ∃ (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → Γ(W, U.1)), RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range f) = a.ker.ideal U ∧ ∃ e : (a ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).toScheme ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of ((Γ(W, U.1) : Type u) ⧸ a.ker.ideal U)), (a ∣_ U.1) ≫ U.1.toSpecΓ = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (a.ker.ideal U))))
